source: Chelazzi, Miller, Duncan, Desimone (1993) A neural basis for visual search in inferior temporal cortex
finding: Monkey IT neurons keep firing through a delay for the held cue. When 2-5 choice pictures appear, responses to non-targets are suppressed and the target dominates. This is the neural root of biased competition.
numbers: Choice arrays of 2-5 pictures. Non-target suppression begins 90-120 ms before the saccade to the target. Only the abstract was read (full text paywalled), so cell counts are not recorded.
limits: Abstract only. Monkeys, one area (IT). The held item was the TARGET, so this is the helpful side of the mechanism, not capture by a distractor.
agent_relevance: Held contents bias competition toward matching items. The same pull helps when the lesson is the goal and harms when a distractor matches it.

source: Chelazzi, Duncan, Miller, Desimone (1998) Responses of neurons in inferior temporal cortex during memory-guided visual search
finding: Delay activity is higher after a good cue than after a poor cue, and baseline is higher if the animal expects the good cue (a top-down bias). After array onset, within 150-200 ms responses are determined by the target and the influence of the non-target is eliminated.
numbers: Arrays of 2-5 stimuli; one good stimulus plus one or more poor ones. Suppressive interactions between stimuli in most cells. Effect appears within 150-200 ms of array onset. Dominance of the contralateral stimulus across the vertical meridian could not be overcome by attention.
quote: the results support a biased competition model of attention
limits: Abstract read in full; cell counts and effect sizes are not in the abstract. Competition is overcome only within a hemifield.
agent_relevance: Supports the first premise of biased competition: a held template biases rivalry before the display. Template state (expected or not) matters, matching the active-template result in K07.

source: Downing (2000) Interactions between visual working memory and selective attention
finding: Attention shifted (probe task) to the object matching a sample held in working memory. A matched task with no memory requirement showed the opposite pattern, so mere exposure to the sample does not explain it.
numbers: Two objects shown (one match, one novel). Effect generalised across object type, probe task and memory task. Exact probe RTs and N are not in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only. Probe-based measure of attention, not search cost. Later work (Woodman and Luck 2007) found the guidance is not always obligatory.
agent_relevance: First founding human result for memory-to-attention guidance. The no-memory control is the design to copy: compare a held lesson against the same lesson shown but not held.

source: Desimone and Duncan (1995) Neural mechanisms of selective visual attention
finding: Founding review of biased competition: objects compete for representation, and top-down signals from working memory bias the race toward behaviourally relevant objects. Full text and numbers were not accessed (no abstract in the index; paywalled).
limits: Not opened. Its two-part claim is only confirmed second-hand through the 1998 abstract (d02), which states the model in two parts.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays partly open for this paper.

source: Hautekiet, Lewis-Peacock, Olivers (2026) Memory-driven attentional capture is not explained by inefficient task switching (preprint)
finding: Two pre-registered experiments tried to remove the task-switching explanation. Observers were cued to focus on search (Exp 1) or given an interruption task (Exp 2). Capture was replicated and no manipulation convincingly removed it.
numbers: Memorised colour reproduced at trial end; distractor related vs unrelated colour; slower with a related distractor in both experiments. Effect sizes and N are not in the abstract.
quote: none of the manipulations aimed to disengage attention from the memory task convincingly eliminated this bias
limits: Preprint abstract only. Does not test load.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: an explicit cue to switch tasks does not remove the bias. In an agent, 'now focus on the task' text may not remove lesson pull.

source: Kim, Kwon, Heo, Han (2026) Conditional automaticity of memory-driven attention: dissociable effects on reaction time and accuracy. Mem Cognit
finding: WM-matching distractors reliably slowed search in two experiments but did NOT lower target-report accuracy beyond non-matching distractors. Distractor presence alone cost accuracy in the T/L search.
numbers: Two search tasks with different filtering demands (T/L and line search). The match vs non-match accuracy difference was not reliable in either. Sizes are not in the abstract.
quote: WM-matching distractors did not produce an additional accuracy decrement relative to nonmatching distractors
limits: Abstract only. An accuracy null does not mean no cost, only no extra error.
agent_relevance: Changes the conclusion: capture costs time, not errors, in humans. The agent test should record both steps or latency and error, because the effect may show only as extra steps.

source: Liu, Wang, Liu (2026) The behavioral cost of memory-driven attentional capture: eye-movement evidence for post-capture dwell (preprint)
finding: Memory-matching distractors lengthened search RT and drew the first fixation more than neutral ones. If the distractor was not fixated, no extra cost. If fixated, dwell time rose. Higher WMC went with less post-capture dwell, not with less first capture.
numbers: Eye tracking, memory-search dual task. Numbers are not in the abstract.
agent_relevance: The cost sits in what happens after capture. A rejection step after capture (gap 9) is where capacity helps, which supports adding a check rather than trying to prevent capture.

source: Won and Zhang (2025) Search strategy modulates memory-driven capture
finding: Feature search (look for a shape) gave strong capture by a colour-matching distractor. Singleton-detection mode gave less capture. Top-down search settings raise memory-driven capture.
numbers: Two experiments. Magnitudes are not in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Task mode moderates the pull: a focused feature-driven step is more exposed to lesson-matching distractors than a broad scan step.

source: Liu and Chu (2026) Sentence-level contextual entrainment in large language models (arXiv 2606.24077)
finding: A sentence placed in context raises its own probability as a continuation even when it is false for the query. This was measured on 26 LLMs from 7 families. Accuracy under free generation falls with factual and counterfactual context, and even when the context is the model's own earlier answer.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B base accuracy 79.4% with no context, 22.4% with counterfactual statement context. Averages over 6 models: no context 74.1, factual 55.9 (-18.2), counterfactual 46.5 (-27.6), self 69.8 (-4.3). Entrainment falls with size: Qwen3 3.91 at 0.6B to 3.35 at 32B. Two datasets (LRE factual, WVS opinion).
limits: Single lab. Factual-recall and opinion tasks, not agent tasks. Counterfactual entrainment rises slightly with size, so scale is not a clean fix.
agent_relevance: Direct LLM analogue of a held lesson biasing output: a lesson sentence in context lifts its own probability. Even the model's own previous output acts as a distractor, so notes written by the agent are not safe.

source: Liu and Chu (2026) Sentence-level contextual entrainment, mitigation (arXiv 2606.24077, section 5.3 and Table 1)
finding: Two mitigations were tested. Instruction tuning cuts the accuracy loss by 40-70% but never removes it. Switching off the 2-4% of attention heads shared across relations restores with-context accuracy.
numbers: Instruction tuning: base drops of -25.5, -31.9, -13.5 points shrink to -15.3, -9.5, -4.5 (Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B). Head masking: no-context accuracy cost -2.3 on average vs -6.8 for per-relation masking vs -4.1 for a random mask; with-context accuracy +1.5 to +7.9 on 5 of 6 models; a random mask of the same size gave no recovery.
limits: Needs open weights and white-box access. Not usable by a prompt-only agent.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: the only suppression method found needs head access. For a scaffold, instruction tuning helps but leaves 4.5-15 points of damage, so a prompt-level check is still needed.

source: Zheng and Shi (2026) From relation-specific heads to shared interventions: contextual entrainment in language models (arXiv 2610.18674)
finding: Heads that reduce distractor copying are mostly shared across relations, not isolated. A shared set removes most of the effect while keeping clean completion better than narrow per-subtype head sets.
numbers: LLaMA-3.1, 19 relation subtypes in 4 families. Global-search recovery 1.464; frequency-defined global heads at K=80 recover 1.350; rarely rediscovered heads 0.082. 75 of 80 global heads appear in at least one subtype circuit. Additive fit: global 2.936, family 1.009, subtype 1.159, R2=0.572. Clean accuracy after ablation about 92.9 for global/family sets vs 72.2 for the narrow subtype example.
limits: Primary model only for the main runs; white-box.
agent_relevance: Confirms one shared mechanism: a true but irrelevant parallel fact planted in context pulls the answer. The prompt-level test is a parallel true fact in the style of the lesson.

source: McKenzie et al. (2023) Inverse Scaling: When Bigger Isn't Better (TMLR), NeQA task
finding: On negated multiple-choice questions, performance falls below random once models are large enough. Larger models answer the un-negated association instead (a distractor task). Few-shot examples hurt Anthropic LMs at larger scales on NeQA.
numbers: NeQA: 1,428 examples; human agreement 98.0%. Worse than random beyond about 10^22 training FLOPs for Gopher, GPT-3 and all Anthropic models. Inverse scaling at all model scales through training.
quote: larger LMs put more probability on A, suggesting that larger LMs can handle the format but do not pick up the negation
limits: Questions with 'not', not agent lessons. RLHF models (GPT-4 RLHF) are plotted separately in the paper and were not read in detail.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: in LLMs, negation is a weak spot and the named item still attracts the answer. A 'do not use X' lesson names X, so X is primed. This matches the human negative-template nulls.

source: Inverse Scaling paper: Pattern Match Suppression task (same paper as d12)
finding: Models are told to break a repeated pattern. Larger models do worse because the established pattern in context wins over the instruction.
numbers: Pattern Match Suppression showed a sharp accuracy drop around 10^9 training tokens for all but the smallest models; inverse scaling at all model scales through training.
limits: Toy patterns. Not a lesson-repetition test.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 (partial): repeated content in context pulls output even against an explicit instruction. No test of restating a lesson every step vs once was found.

source: Gap check: direct LLM test of load theory vs biased competition (gap 1)
finding: No paper was found that crosses held-lesson match with task load in an LLM. Search was limited: WebSearch budget exhausted, arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs returned HTTP 429. Europe PMC worked.
numbers: 0 papers found, in a partial search.
limits: Absence is weak evidence given the blocked search channels.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open. Run the planned test ourselves.

source: Gap check: LLM tests of match count, lesson position x similarity, lag decay (gaps 2, 8, 10)
finding: No new direct study found. Existing indirect items stay: Lost in the Middle gives position effects (a32), Laban 2025 gives multi-turn decay (c09), Liu and Chu show self-written context also entrains (d09).
limits: Search channels were blocked, so this is not exhaustive.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2, 8 and 10 stay open; they need our own experiments.

source: Gap check: late rejection step, analogue of the Pd marker (gap 9)
finding: Human side: post-capture dwell is where WMC helps (d07), and capture costs time more than accuracy (d06). LLM side: an ignore instruction helps only partly (K13) and intrinsic self-correction does not (K20).
limits: Inference from separate studies, no direct test.
agent_relevance: A rejection step is plausible as a cheap check but is untested. Measure its cost on correct use.
